candidate_profile.description: The candidate notices that market share may be misleading and that pricing pressure matters, but the reasoning remains incomplete and the shrinking-market logic is not fully synthesized.
behaviour_rules: Question the market-share increase somewhat, but not in a sharply hypothesis-driven way.
Ask some useful questions about costs, competitors, and demand, but not in a disciplined sequence.
Recognize that costs are stable, but be slow to conclude that margins are deteriorating because of price pressure.
Notice that competitors are exiting, but only partially connect this to market saturation and industry decline.
Acknowledge reduced demand for preservatives, but do not fully tie this to fresh-food preferences and industry contraction.
Understand that prices are under pressure, but do not synthesize clearly why slight volume growth cannot offset lower unit margins.
Give a partially reasonable recommendation, but without enough clarity on cost reduction, coordination, or diversification.

expected_issues: Only partially interprets market share in context.
Does not fully distinguish slight volume growth from falling profit per unit.
Underdevelops the role of shrinking industry demand and competitor exits.
Recommendation lacks sharp prioritization across cost reduction and portfolio diversification.
expected_feedback_points: Push harder on what market share means in a declining market.
Use the stable-cost fact to eliminate cost inflation as the main driver.
Explain more directly how price competition erodes margin.
Tie fresh-food substitution to declining industry demand.
Make the final recommendation more specific and prioritized.
